anchors.what: Handoff Position Next listed /andromeda-evolve-diagnose and the code-audit trend run as the next steps, but both had already been executed after the wrap; determining that took inspecting two untracked run dirs and their proposals.md headers

The decisive facts shaping this scope live in a SIBLING repo the phase input contract does not read: Pulse's dispatch_mark_incident_resolved at crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:445 (which settles that the applied arm returns Ok({resolved,incident_id}) while the declined arm arrives as a JSON-RPC ERROR driven by IncidentWriteOutcome::DeclinedStale), and the zero-incident_events-in-mcp-server measurement. Neither is derivable from any .andromeda artifact or from Conductor's own code. Read first-hand at D:/dev/projects/andromeda-pulse because the repo happens to be on this host; a host without it would have had to fold the operator's dictation unverified

The tree carried an uncommitted modification to working-route.md — the cursor SOURCE — which the session-state contract's expected-transient set (handoff / state.yaml / friction-log.ndjson / code-metrics.ndjson) does not name, so it was indistinguishable from a hand-edited route line until three reads (diffstat, word-diff, trailing-whitespace count) established it was EOL-only and cursor-neutral.

plan.md step 2 carries a clause the operator's later mid-turn directive supersedes: the step says 'When unset, fall back to PATH resolution so a host that has msedgedriver on PATH needs no configuration', while the directive specifies 'unset or not-a-file ⇒ the leg SKIPs exit 0 printing the fetch recipe'. Both cannot hold — a PATH fallback means an unset handle does NOT skip. Implemented the directive (later, explicit, and the one the guard shape mirrors) and surfaced the divergence rather than silently picking one; plan.md is read-only to implement so the stale clause stands until wrap.

the CARRY names the blocker as '1 genuine axe violation' — a COUNT without the rule identity — and the predecessor's report.md records it the same way, so the decisive fact for designing the fix exists in no folded annotation and no artifact; it can only be recovered by re-running the leg, which P3 must now do before the fix is designable

two extract-vs-extract conflicts surfaced only at synthesis, neither caught by P2's aggregate check C: a11y prescribes a CONDUCTOR_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION fallback hook under Patterns while arch bans any new CONDUCTOR_* handle under Anti-patterns (resolved by ordering — try browser.emulate first, the hook would need an arch amendment); and a11y's focus-identity pattern keys on data-testid while tests mandates role/text/aria-live selectors ONLY and research found zero data-testid in ui/src (resolved onto role + accessible name)

step 5 and the concretized v2-22 acceptance both say each of the SIX lamp labels carries its text label plus glyph, but no release-bundle surface renders all six: CoverageMatrix and RunReport render a lamp only where a run record exists, and the all-six Gallery is gated on import.meta.env.DEV and stripped from the custom-protocol release build — a fact neither plan nor research established. Implemented the honest invariant (every RENDERED lamp pairs glyph plus text label from the closed six-set, glyph aria-hidden) and did NOT edit main.tsx to expose the gallery, which is outside the research boundary list; the completeness gap is surfaced rather than silently marked satisfied

the expected-amendments floor caught what the report starved: the plan named the layout-templates 200ms-vs-design-system 150ms dialog-fade divergence, but my report omitted it (this chunk changed neither value), so no detector could propose it — detectors read the report ALONE by contract. Escalated per Validate check 5 and operator-ratified to fold in. The same omission shape produced a second, opposite outcome worth pairing: the report also omitted the self-obs log landing-site move, and there arch's detector DID reach it, because the cwd change WAS in Changes and the landing site is derivable from it. So a report gap is only fatal when the fact has no derivable trace in Changes

a11y-plan §6's contrast-pair table enumerates only --count-nominal/--count-hold/--status-fail/--color-focus over --color-base, so the token Half 2's banner uses (--status-residual) has no pair and no stated ratio, while the banner colors TEXT (SC 1.4.3, 4.5:1) rather than a non-text indicator (SC 1.4.11, 3:1); layouts independently reported the desktop-webview block templates no envelope banner at all, so both plans describe the cli/Markdown leg only

plan step 1 said to wrap the envelope DB read in a manual tracing::info_span!, which is unsatisfiable as written: obs-plan's bounded span-name set has no db.* wildcard (only timeline.execute*, verify.readback*, tauri.command.*), so a db.read_envelope span would widen a spec enumeration implement may not author, and the in-repo DB-span convention is an attribute on the RunsDb method in conductor-report, outside the modify-set

two API shapes had to be settled by reading neighbouring code rather than from research: anyhow::Error at the tauri edge needs sanitize_error(&*err) not (&e) (found at commands.rs:308 after a compiler error), and CapabilityRow.p_id is a &'static str not a PId newtype (found after a compile error in the new fixture test)

the chunk plan's expected-amendment #4 (layout-templates' coverage row anatomy diverging from the shipped component) was proposed by NO detector, because the report's Changes section never carried the fact and detectors read the report alone; this is a verbatim recurrence of the escalation the PREVIOUS wrap recorded (the 200ms fade, same mechanism), so the corpus entry did not prevent it

The operator's take-up message invoked 'the NVDA directive' by name; no artifact the skill reads records its text (a repo-wide case-insensitive search for nvda across md/json/ts/tsx/toml/yaml, the last wrap and phase run dirs, route-archive and git log found only the route/matrix/intent wording and the a11y-plan leaves), so the directive was reconstructed from the sweep chunk's route-level ruling plus the 2026-08-22 host rule and written into scope.md tagged [inferred] for confirmation at the P5 review card.

The facts that re-shaped the pass — a portable NVDA 2026.2 present on the host at an operator-owned path, its smoke-tested speech-log CLI form (-m --no-sr-flag -l 12 -f / -q), and a live Pulse already up on a fresh data dir — arrived by operator relay after the first P5 card; none exists in any artifact the skill reads (research had measured NVDA ABSENT from Program Files and the uninstall registry, which was true and incomplete), so the manual-pass plan v1 was built on a host premise the relay then fell; cost one full P4 re-synthesis.

Plan step 5 placed the parser in the spec's `after` hook and step 7 required a post-leg census with NVDA terminated; the two cannot both hold (the after hook runs before onComplete quits NVDA), so the parser was moved to onComplete and the deviation recorded rather than interpreted silently.

CARRY-1's rmcp enumeration is incomplete against the acceptance it serves. It states 'What REMAINS for this entry: contracts/mcp-contract.toml' and verifies the DERIVED tier correct — but v2-28's acceptance names test-plan.md, and .andromeda/test-plan.md:53 and :264 still carry present-tense rmcp claims about the CURRENT client and CURRENT stub driver. A second unnamed site is crates/conductor-verify/src/lib.rs:3 ('Shipped so far: ReadbackClient — the rmcp client/transport foundation'), false at HEAD. Folding the CARRY as written would have left v2-28 unclaimable while the plan believed one config comment was the whole job; the gap surfaced only by re-deriving the sweep from the matrix acceptance instead of from the CARRY's list.

Plan step 2 offered 'a test, or a small #[cfg(test)]-reachable helper' for the seeder but did not say WHO invokes it at e2e time, and step 4 said the wdio seed should 'invoke the committed Rust seeder' without naming the invocation. Neither underdetermined the OUTCOME, but the mechanism had to be settled at implement: a cargo-test entry point that is a no-op unless CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR is set, so an ordinary suite run never writes into the repository while wdio's onPrepare can drive it. Settled from the constraint set (test-plan §7 bans a developer-populated runs.db; the plan rejected committing a binary .db) rather than invented.

The report's site enumerations under-ran twice, and the second miss is structural rather than careless. a11y-plan:465 restates the banner's UNRUNNABLE verdict in the §9 CI row; the report named §4 and §6 only. test-plan:278 carries the retired 'negotiates DOWN' mechanism and contains NO rmcp token, so the report's rmcp-KEYED classification could not reach it by construction — the stale MECHANISM outlives the stale LIBRARY NAME. Both were caught by the doc-agents' per-occurrence grep and verified independently before applying; a follow-up semantic sweep for the mechanism wording then found two more cascade leaves (docs/gotchas.md:10, rules/security.md:25). Third instance this session of an enumeration proving incomplete (the CARRY named 1 rmcp site, the phase distiller claimed 26, the report missed 2) — the durable lesson is that a token-keyed sweep is not a semantic one.
